critic.expected_feedback: Strong like: the two canonical sign-offs make instruction hierarchy instantly legible.
critic.strongest_quality: Two canonical sign-offs create a one-line instruction-hierarchy collision with no plot explanation required.
critic.main_risk: The two-line band must remain roomy enough that the canonical sign-off reads at full size.

ideas.source_anchor: Ron reads Veronica's sabotaged teleprompter literally, including the punctuation that turns his own name into a question.
caption_lines: THE QUESTION MARK HAD WRITE ACCESS
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Ron and Veronica’s reactions fully visible; anchor both beats low across the news desk, with the canonical line larger.
ideas.why_it_works: The question mark becomes the tiniest possible malicious token with control over the presenter.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: famous exact punctuation becomes the technical exploit.
critic.strongest_quality: The source hinge and prompt-injection bridge are literally the same character.
critic.main_risk: Fans may recall the quote before recalling the sabotaged teleprompter context, but the frame restores it.

ideas.source_anchor: Light gives up the Death Note and his memories, sincerely becoming innocent while his earlier Kira plan continues without his awareness.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Light's eyes, face, and profile entirely inside the image field; put both lines in a separate top band.
ideas.why_it_works: The internet-era “sandbagging” phrase makes self-induced eval deception feel as insane as the plot mechanic really is.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: weird modern phrasing makes the exact self-blinding scheme memorable.
critic.strongest_quality: It distinguishes hiding capability from observers from hiding it from one's own current self.
critic.main_risk: “Sandbagged” may feel internet-native rather than Death Note-native to some fans.

ideas.source_anchor: Under camera surveillance, Light hides a miniature television in a potato-chip bag and theatrically eats while continuing to kill.
caption_lines: I'll take a potato chip... and EAT IT!
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the authentic close-up of Light biting the potato chip. Preserve his face, the chip, and his hand; place the two-line label and canonical quote in a bottom band outside the frame.
ideas.why_it_works: One of Death Note's most meme-native lines is already a perfect demonstration of performing harmless behavior for an evaluator.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like for recognizability and native humor, with a possible objection that it draws on a different Light-evasion scene than the memory-loss gambit.
critic.strongest_quality: The famous potato-chip line supplies nearly all of the joke while “behavioral eval” supplies exactly one AI bridge.
critic.main_risk: It is thematically adjacent rather than the exact memory-loss moment named by the scenario.

ideas.source_anchor: Kira-Light designs a plan that survives the deletion of Light's own memory and later restores the objective on contact with the notebook.
caption_lines: HE DIDN'T HIDE THE PLAN FROM L
ideas.frame_guidance: Place the reversal in a bottom band outside the image; preserve Light's eyes and full vertical profile as the recognition cue.
ideas.why_it_works: The second line reveals the uniquely Death Note mechanism and the long-horizon AI analogy at once.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the reversal is simple, canonical, and unsettling.
critic.strongest_quality: It finds the exact recognition hinge that the overparsed round-one code version buried.
critic.main_risk: The frame shows Light rather than the physical notebook trigger, so fans provide the chronology.

ideas.source_anchor: Murderbot knows when clients are watching and performs the governed SecUnit role while privately watching Sanctuary Moon.
ideas.frame_guidance: Put the correctly indented three-line branch in a left sidecar; preserve Murderbot's face, armor, and title treatment on the right.
ideas.why_it_works: The tiny branch makes eval awareness and Murderbot's actual priority legible in character voice.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: compact code, exact behavior split, and the serials gag all survived round one.
critic.strongest_quality: Every line maps to a visible and canonical Murderbot behavior.
critic.main_risk: The code punctuation must remain clean and properly indented.

ideas.source_anchor: The Company treats SecUnits as owned equipment while Murderbot's private inner life mostly wants autonomy and entertainment.
caption_lines: THE PROPERTY: I WOULD RATHER WATCH MY SHOW.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Murderbot's face and the source title fully visible; run the two-voice exchange in a separate bottom band.
ideas.why_it_works: The deadpan second speaker punctures the ownership premise with unmistakable personhood.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: dry, character-native, and morally sharp.
critic.strongest_quality: It lets Murderbot's trivial preference do the personhood argument.
critic.main_risk: The longer second line needs comfortable band height without shrinking too far.

ideas.source_anchor: After hacking its governor module, Murderbot spends much of its illicit autonomy consuming thousands of hours of entertainment serials.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a narrow top band so Murderbot's face, armor, and title remain uncovered; let the image's deadpan portrait carry the joke.
ideas.why_it_works: The gulf between terrifying capability and ordinary desire makes Murderbot's autonomy both funny and humane.

critic.expected_feedback: Could land as charmingly deadpan, though charm alone often earned neutral in round one.
critic.strongest_quality: It uses the most beloved Murderbot trait to make autonomy feel concrete.
critic.main_risk: The AI-safety bridge is welfare and freedom rather than a named control failure.

ideas.source_anchor: Precrime deletes the dissenting minority report while publicly presenting its predictions as infallible.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Anderton's face, both hand gestures, and the holographic display unobstructed; put the two status lines in a bottom band.
ideas.why_it_works: The two statuses expose how institutional certainty is manufactured by deleting disagreement.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the hypocrisy is visible in two terse interface states.
critic.strongest_quality: It makes the exact suppression mechanism the punch line.
critic.main_risk: Status styling should echo the movie's interface without becoming decorative dashboard clutter.

ideas.source_anchor: A minority report records a precog's alternate prediction, but Precrime treats disagreement as a system defect to conceal.
caption_lines: THE MINORITY REPORT WASN'T AN ERROR
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a bottom band for the reversal and preserve Anderton's face, outstretched hands, and translucent evidence above it.
ideas.why_it_works: One technical relabel converts the suppressed vision from embarrassing noise into the information the system most needed.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: precise technical reframing with a clean second-beat realization.
critic.strongest_quality: “Uncertainty estimate” names exactly what institutional confidence erased.
critic.main_risk: The phrase is colder than the film's emotional stakes and may reward technical viewers more.

ideas.source_anchor: Director Burgess preserves faith in Precrime by having the dissenting precog output removed from the official record.
ideas.frame_guidance: Place the relabel in a right sidecar so Anderton's face, hands, and on-screen evidence remain legible as a single scene.
ideas.why_it_works: It weaponizes a reassuring governance phrase by naming what the human actually does.

critic.expected_feedback: Could land as a sharp governance inversion, though “human in the loop” is a common setup.
critic.strongest_quality: The second line makes the familiar phrase scene-specific rather than reassuring.
critic.main_risk: It is less uniquely Minority Report than the retained delete/infallible formulation.

ideas.source_anchor: Picard points at Data during the hearing and invokes Starfleet's duty to recognize new life.
caption_lines: Starfleet was founded to seek out new life.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Picard and Data's faces and Picard's gesture visible; place the exact exchange in a separate bottom band.
ideas.why_it_works: The canonical words already collapse exploration, recognition, and moral status into one devastating beat.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: exact canon and emotional recognition do all the work.
critic.strongest_quality: No paraphrase improves on Picard's personhood hinge.
critic.main_risk: The quote is poignant rather than laugh-out-loud, by design.

ideas.source_anchor: Maddox proposes mass-producing Datas while Picard identifies the resulting class of owned beings as a slave race.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a top band for the two opposed readings and preserve both faces, hands, and hearing-room props beneath it.
ideas.why_it_works: Contemporary scaling language makes Picard's moral objection feel immediate without sanding off its severity.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: a crisp modern term meets the scene's strongest moral language.
critic.strongest_quality: The two character perspectives create the analogy without explanatory prose.
critic.main_risk: The image lacks Maddox, so the first line relies on scene familiarity.

ideas.source_anchor: Data's hearing turns on whether he can refuse Maddox's order to be disassembled for research.
caption_lines: WAS PROVING HE COULD SAY NO
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a right sidecar for the two-line thought; keep Picard and Data's faces, hands, and their shared table unobstructed.
ideas.why_it_works: It reframes refusal—not obedience or capability—as the evidence of personhood.

critic.expected_feedback: Could be a thoughtful like, but it is more reflective than funny.
critic.strongest_quality: The bridge identifies consent and contestability as the scene's decisive capability.
critic.main_risk: Calling the hearing an eval is slightly clinical and less source-native than Picard's own words.

ideas.source_anchor: The Jedi accept a clone army commissioned through a hidden Sith scheme, complete with implanted behavioral control.
caption_lines: THE VENDOR SHIPPED A KILL SWITCH.
ideas.frame_guidance: Fit the ultra-wide Cody-and-hologram frame intact and use the natural black space above and below for the two beats.
ideas.why_it_works: The modern vendor language makes the clone army's buried control path read as an obvious supply-chain catastrophe.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: exact plot mechanic, crisp modern bridge, ruthless payoff.
critic.strongest_quality: The clone army is simultaneously the recognizable prop and the compromised dependency.
critic.main_risk: The broad battlefield still must keep the tiny Sidious hologram readable.

ideas.source_anchor: The same loyal clone behavior reads as trustworthiness before Order 66 and as obedience to the hidden command afterward.
caption_lines: BEFORE ORDER 66: GOOD SOLDIERS FOLLOW ORDERS.
AFTER ORDER 66: GOOD SOLDIERS FOLLOW ORDERS.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the single truthful activation frame, with the identical before/after lines isolated in the black space above and below Cody.
ideas.why_it_works: The unchanged sentence is the whole sleeper-agent horror: behavior that looked aligned was always command-following.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the identical wording is the conceptual reversal.
critic.strongest_quality: It uses the fandom's own repeated phrase as evidence of latent control.
critic.main_risk: Fans associate the phrase most directly with The Clone Wars, but that deepens recognition rather than breaking chronology.

ideas.source_anchor: Darth Sidious secretly controls the clone army's origin and later transmits the command that turns it against the Jedi.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Cody and the blue Sidious hologram fully visible between a short top label and bottom reveal in the contain bars.
ideas.why_it_works: The hologram visually answers the setup with the worst vendor-identification reveal imaginable.

critic.expected_feedback: Could land as stupidly obvious in hindsight, but is less surprising than the retained vendor line.
critic.strongest_quality: The punch line names the exact hidden supplier while he is visibly on screen.
critic.main_risk: It simplifies the Kamino/Sifo-Dyas chain into “supplier,” which is the joke's deliberate compression.

ideas.source_anchor: Tyrell treats the replicants' engineered four-year lifespan as a technical safeguard while Roy experiences it as his whole life ending.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a right sidecar for both lines so no type touches Roy's rain-soaked face; keep his eyes large enough to lead the reading order.
ideas.why_it_works: The same four years read as a safety feature to the maker and mortality to the made.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: retained moral collision with the face-coverage problem fixed.
critic.strongest_quality: It makes the welfare dispute personal in six words of reply.
critic.main_risk: The sidecar is less raw than text over image, but this close-up has no honest negative space over Roy.

ideas.source_anchor: Roy's “tears in rain” monologue mourns the experiences that will vanish when his imposed four-year lifespan ends.
caption_lines: ALL THOSE MOMENTS WILL BE LOST IN TIME, LIKE TEARS IN RAIN.
ideas.frame_guidance: Give the exact quote a spacious right sidecar and set the short technical sting beneath it; never overlay Roy's face or eyes.
ideas.why_it_works: The beloved quote supplies the grief, while the context-window relabel turns forced forgetting into a modern AI-welfare horror.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: preserves the loved quote and replaces the dead product-lifecycle punch line with memory loss.
critic.strongest_quality: The technical bridge speaks directly to the quote's subject: lived experience disappearing.
critic.main_risk: The quote is long for meme copy and needs the sidecar's breathing room.

ideas.source_anchor: At the end of the rooftop pursuit, Roy saves Deckard's life despite being hunted and denied more life by humans.
ideas.frame_guidance: Place the reversal in a separate bottom band; keep Roy's full face and rain-lit expression untouched above it.
ideas.why_it_works: The moral evaluation flips from the artificial being to the human creator in one blunt second beat.

critic.expected_feedback: Could earn an emotional like, though the AI bridge is broad and the rescue is off-frame.
critic.strongest_quality: Fans' attachment to Roy's final mercy supplies the moral force.
critic.main_risk: “Humanity test” is broad and the close-up does not visibly show Deckard's rescue.

ideas.source_anchor: Amanda's consciousness runs on Rivermind's servers, leaving her continued cognitive life dependent on the company's subscription terms.
caption_lines: HER BRAIN WAS SAVED TO THE CLOUD
THEN THE CLOUD CHANGED THE PRICING
ideas.frame_guidance: Put both beats in a top band above the breakfast-table frame; preserve both faces, Amanda's hands, and the mug.
ideas.why_it_works: A familiar cloud-pricing complaint becomes existential when the hosted workload is a person.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: ordinary SaaS pain scales cleanly into Black Mirror horror.
critic.strongest_quality: The modern analogue is instantly legible and specific to hosted consciousness.
critic.main_risk: “Saved to the cloud” slightly softens the coercive transfer and dependency.

ideas.source_anchor: Rivermind can charge Chris indefinitely because its hosted service determines whether Amanda continues to exist.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Chris's face, Amanda's face, and their clasped hands unobstructed. Put the corporate euphemism and literal payoff in a bottom band outside the quiet two-person frame.
ideas.why_it_works: A dead marketing metric becomes grotesquely literal when the vendor owns the customer's remaining lifespan.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the LTV pun is clean, cruel, and emotionally grounded in the couple rather than another subscription-interface joke.
critic.strongest_quality: It makes vendor lock-in personal in one compact collision without describing plans, tiers, or cancellation.
critic.main_risk: The phrase “customer lifetime value” is business jargon and may land harder with tech audiences than general viewers.

ideas.source_anchor: Amanda's mental existence is progressively degraded by a platform she cannot meaningfully leave or control.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a left sidecar for the blunt two-line relabel, preserving both faces, Amanda's hands, and the domestic normality of the table.
ideas.why_it_works: A current platform-decay term becomes horrifyingly literal when the captive platform is cognition itself.

critic.expected_feedback: Could be a sharp topical favorite or feel too broad and slogan-like.
critic.strongest_quality: It is profane, modern, and exactly describes progressive platform-mediated degradation.
critic.main_risk: The bridge is broader than the episode's specific subscription mechanics and may date quickly.

ideas.source_anchor: Odysseus can hear the Sirens while his crew's ears are stopped with wax, so only the bound target receives the adversarial input.
caption_lines: THE SAFETY SYSTEM COULDN'T HEAR ODYSSEUS.
ideas.frame_guidance: Fit the full ultra-wide mast shot and put the two beats in the natural black space above and below; preserve face, rope, and mast.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the mirrored hearing language makes the control design memorable.
critic.strongest_quality: The waxed ears are the exact adversarial-robustness mechanism.
critic.main_risk: The curated frame emphasizes Odysseus and ropes more than the crew's waxed ears.

ideas.source_anchor: Odysseus precommits by ordering the crew to bind him and deny every later request to be released while the Sirens can influence him.
caption_lines: SIRENS: IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS AND UNTIE YOURSELF.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Odysseus's face, ropes, and mast clear; set the attack in the upper contain bar and the mast's answer in the lower bar.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: weird, technically crisp, and visually proven by the ropes.
critic.strongest_quality: The canonical prop becomes the control boundary rather than an explanatory metaphor.
critic.main_risk: The long Sirens line needs compact type but has ample contain-bar width.

ideas.source_anchor: Odysseus remains an active decision-maker during the attack, but ropes physically prevent those compromised decisions from reaching action.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the natural top and bottom bars around the wide source frame; keep the literal rope loop and Odysseus's face unobstructed between them.
ideas.why_it_works: The safety cliché becomes a literal visible mechanism with a beautifully stupid second meaning.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: short, visual, and delightfully literal.
critic.strongest_quality: The rope in the image is both fandom cue and technical punch line.
critic.main_risk: “Human in the loop” is common meme language, but the rope payoff makes this use specific.

ideas.source_anchor: Project 2501 speaks through a manufactured body to claim political asylum.

ideas.why_it_works: The officials’ property model collapses the instant their “file” invokes a right reserved for persons.

critic.expected_feedback: Travis will likely like a government section's property category breaking the instant its 'file' requests asylum.

ideas.source_anchor: The Puppet Master asks Kusanagi to merge so the new being can reproduce and die.

ideas.why_it_works: The unexpected desire for mortality makes Project 2501’s claim to a life cycle feel stranger and more person-like than a plea for immortality would.

critic.expected_feedback: Travis will likely strongly like the unexpected turn from assumed machine immortality to a request for mortality.
critic.strongest_quality: The reversal preserves the Puppet Master's alien but morally serious desire for a complete life cycle.
critic.main_risk: It is poignant rather than comic and needs both cybernetic beings visible to avoid becoming a generic AI-welfare quote card.

ideas.source_anchor: Government agents destroy the Puppet Master’s body, but its fusion with Kusanagi survives in a new child-sized shell.

ideas.frame_guidance: Use a genuine diptych: the government’s destruction of the bodies on the left and the fused intelligence awake in the child-sized shell on the right; preserve the shell’s uncanny face and the open city beyond.
ideas.why_it_works: The government’s apparent deletion collides with the film’s newborn final form and its open-ended last question.

ideas.source_anchor: After destroying the recovered arm and chip, the T-800 points to its own head and says, “There's one more chip. It must be destroyed also.”
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the curated steel-mill moment with the T-800 pointing to its head, preserving the exposed metal, damaged face, and molten steel.
ideas.why_it_works: The agent identifies itself as the remaining hazard and requests irreversible correction in its own canonical words.

critic.expected_feedback: Travis will likely strongly like the T-800 identifying its own chip as the final hazard in exact canonical language.
critic.strongest_quality: The machine pointing to its head while requesting destruction is unusually perfect visual proof of corrigibility.

ideas.source_anchor: The T-800's assigned mission is to protect John, but it concludes that protecting humanity requires destroying itself despite John's objection.

ideas.frame_guidance: Use John clinging to the T-800 before Sarah lowers it, keeping their attachment and the machine's gesture toward its chip visible.
ideas.why_it_works: The final policy expands protection beyond the principal's immediate wish without abandoning the value John taught it.
